Apple CEO Tim Cook posted a witty message on X, sharing a video showing the "Pokémon" team visiting Apple Park, with Pikachu roaming around. Check it out below.

Pikachu visits Apple Park

Apple hosted the "Pokémon" team at Apple Park today, and they took the opportunity to have some fun.

In the video shared on X, Tim Cook jokingly mentioned that the day's agenda was to introduce the "Pokémon" team to new CEO John Ternus, "chat about games," and "politely ask Pikachu not to go near the pond."

Cook also said: "We managed to do two out of three things."

The accompanying video shows Pikachu roaming around Apple Park, stretching its legs to pick an apple from under an apple tree, and eventually heading towards the pond. Later, Cook, Ternus, and "The Pokémon Company" CEO Tsunekazu Ishihara joined in.

Although neither Apple nor "The Pokémon Company" revealed further details about the visit, the video is quite fun and worth 30 seconds of your time.

The meeting between Apple and "The Pokémon Company" CEOs came just a few weeks after Sensor Tower reported a 4.5% year-over-year decline in mobile game revenue for the second quarter of 2026.

The meeting between Apple and "The Pokémon Company" came just a few weeks after they acknowledged that weakening mobile game performance had begun to weigh on App Store growth.

During the Q3 2026 earnings call, Apple CFO Kevan Parekh specifically mentioned "headwinds in mobile gaming" as one of the factors affecting App Store performance that quarter. To learn more, check back here.
